phase_name: Strict-mode migration batch A (highest-risk state mutators)

objectives.note: Found and fixed 2 -e-hostile VAR=$(cmd) assignments (dry-run and real transform branches) that would have silently short-circuited past the documented exit-3 error message under -e. Fixed via the standard `VAR=$(cmd) || status=$?` guard. Verified with a live mktemp-fixture exercise (valid write, dry-run valid, dry-run invalid filter exit 3, real invalid filter exit 3 with file left untouched) plus test-state-write-concurrency.sh (9/9) and test-state-write-regen-timing.sh (3/3), both green. Committed separately (task 988 phase 6.1).

Full -e-hostility audit of all 1644 lines. Found three hazard classes: (1) ~50 bare `VAR=$(jq/ps/stat/cat/date/find ...)` command-substitution assignments with no explicit `||` guard; (2) 4 bare non-assignment statements whose failure was tolerated (`mkdir -p` x2, `cat > tmp_file`, `rm -f`/`rm -rf` x2); (3) a distinct and easy-to-miss `[ cond ] && action` bare-statement class (e.g. `[ -n "$x" ] && echo ... >&2`, `[ cond ] && continue`, `[ "$LOADED" = true ] && return 0`) that is `-e`-hostile whenever the CONDITION is false (the common case), not just when the guarded action fails -- this class was not called out by name in the plan and is worth flagging for the remaining Phase 6/7 files. Also found and fixed one true `VAR=$(cmd); status=$?` anti-pattern in cmd_acquire_retry (captured_stderr/rc), converted to the sanctioned `if VAR=$(cmd); then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi` idiom. Fixed the two heaviest-reused leaf helpers (read_holder_field, session_registry_dir) at their single definition site so every call site inherited the fix, rather than guarding each of their ~15 call sites individually. Verified via 27/27 run-all.sh (one pre-existing, documented-unrelated flaky failure in test-claude-refresh-matcher.sh reproduced identically both before and after this file's changes -- confirmed not a regression) plus an extensive live mktemp-fixture exercise covering every subcommand and every documented exit code: acquire (fresh/same-session-reentry/refuse/stale-override), acquire-retry (budget exhaustion), heartbeat, release (wrong-session warn, correct-session), check (free/held-fresh/held-stale), reap (dry-run, corrupt-holder skip, real reap), session-register/session-list/session-heartbeat/session-reap/session-release, scope-acquire/scope-release, commit-acquire/commit-release, and init-marker (fresh create + already-exists path). One pre-existing, zero-caller behavior quirk found in cmd_init_marker (a second call after a first successful call silently overwrites rather than returning 1, since init_dir is no longer held) -- confirmed present byte-for-byte in the pre-migration committed version via git diff, so NOT introduced by this migration; left unfixed as out of scope (init-marker has no live callers anywhere in agent-system/extensions/**) and flagged here as a residual finding for a future task.

Full -e-hostility audit of all 292 lines. Found and fixed the same `VAR=$(cmd); status=$?` anti-pattern as task-lock.sh's cmd_acquire_retry, twice: the primary `git commit` call and its index.lock-contention retry both captured `commit_output=$(git commit ...)` followed by a bare `commit_exit=$?` on the next line -- since git commit's documented exit code 1 ("nothing to commit") is a routine, non-error outcome, a bare failing assignment there would have aborted the script under -e before the retry logic, the NOTE message, or this script's own documented exit-code contract could run. Fixed both sites via the sanctioned `if VAR=$(cmd); then status=0; else status=$?; fi` idiom. No other hazards found: every other bare-looking command substitution/pipeline in this file is already the condition of an if/while, or already carries an explicit `||` guard; the `[ cond ] && action` bare-statement class found in task-lock.sh does not occur here. Verified via 27/27 run-all.sh plus a live git-fixture exercise (isolated mktemp -d git repo, not the real repo) covering: a normal commit, the nothing-to-commit exit-1 path (the exact hazard just fixed -- confirmed the NOTE message now prints and exit 1 is returned cleanly), the V3 exclude-only refusal (exit 2), the V2 unmatched-pathspec drop-with-warning path, and the --honest-index-rows addendum.

Full -e-hostility audit of all 538 lines. Found and fixed the SAME critical `VAR=$(cmd); status=$?` anti-pattern as git-commit-scoped.sh's git-commit capture, at the script's single most important line: `verdicts=$(jq -n -c ... 2>&1)` followed by a bare `jq_exit=$?` on the next line -- a jq failure (documented routine exit code 2) would have aborted the script under -e before jq_exit could be captured or the clean ERROR message could print. Fixed via the sanctioned if/then/else idiom. Also found and guarded 4 bare `VAR=$(jq/paste ...)` assignments feeding the degraded-critical-path-file warning path (critical_raw_json, critical_expanded_json), the session-registry read (sessions_json), and the candidates-array build (candidates_json) -- each already had a downstream empty/null check that needed to actually run rather than being bypassed by an early -e abort. No `[ cond ] && action` bare-statement hazards found (unlike task-lock.sh). Verified via 27/27 run-all.sh (1 confirmed pre-existing unrelated flaky failure on first run, clean on immediate rerun) plus a live fixture exercise (isolated mktemp -d specs/ + critical-paths.json) covering: a normal file_scope_collision defer, an edge-excluded non-collision admit, an unknown-task admit, 3 usage-error paths (no args, non-integer task_number, missing state.json -- all exit 2), a self_modifying co-dispatched defer, and -- directly exercising the exact hazards just fixed -- a malformed critical-paths.json (degraded warning + graceful continue, not abort), a missing critical-paths.json (same), and a malformed state.json (jq failure -> clean ERROR message + exit 2, not a bash errexit trace).
